evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Characters Database), CUHK
evidence.field: 女: oracle-bone and bronze form account
evidence.text: The database analyzes oracle-bone and bronze 女 as a kneeling woman, with knees and toes down, seated on the heels and hands crossed at the chest. It says later bronze forms simplify the seated posture. This is a source’s graphic interpretation; it does not establish household work or social symbolism from the shape alone.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 女

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Characters Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The database reports oracle-bone uses for female, 母, 毋, 每/悔 and place names; bronze uses include female, 母, second-person 汝 and 如. These are reported readings or graph uses, separate from the graph’s shape development. The page gives examples but this research did not independently date and examine each inscription context.

evidence.source: 常用漢字二百字探源（金真姬）
evidence.field: 女 entry: form history and cited uses
evidence.text: The entry describes oracle-bone and early bronze 女 as a side-view kneeling woman with hands engaged in an activity; it says later bronze forms lose the recognizable kneeling posture, the small-seal form continues that shape, and by the Warring States period the original depiction is obscure. It cites oracle-bone examples for female and a reading as 母. The cited catalog numbers do not, by themselves, establish a precise date for each inscription.
evidence.title: 常用漢字二百字探源

evidence.text: The individual record labels a 女 oracle-bone form 前7.36.1 and 合3298, alongside the regular-script 女. It supports the record identity and source label; it does not itself date the inscription or establish a semantic sequence.

evidence.field: 女-seal.svg file description, source and licensing
evidence.text: The description identifies the file as a modern vector depiction of 女 in Shuowen seal-script style and lists paleographic reference sources. Its licensing section releases the SVG representation to the public domain. This is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph. The page exposes an original-file link, but the web fetch of that link returned a cache-miss error during this research.

search_audit.outcome: Inspected CUHK, the cited paleographic dictionary PDF, Sinica’s form-evolution page and individual form record, Xiaoxuetang rights page, and a Commons seal-script file description. The original-file fetch for the seal redraw failed with a cache miss; the failed oracle and bronze image URLs in the supplied acquisition findings were excluded.

gaps: No sound component applies: 女 is analyzed in the cited sources as an independent pictograph, not a phonetic compound.

The sources support an early female-related reading and report several other early graph uses, but this research did not establish dated contextual attestations or a semantic chronology for daughter, marriage, feminine, pronoun, or the reported loans. Gloss lists and graphic change do not establish those links.

Accounts vary in how they describe the posture and hand position. The specific breast interpretation and claim that the modern form is reversed relative to oracle-bone forms were not verified in the inspected references.

The exact Sinica rights page opened without readable terms in the web tool, so no Sinica image is proposed. The Commons seal redraw’s page states public-domain licensing, but its original-file fetch failed; the supplied Commons oracle and bronze candidates are unavailable following their earlier 404s.
No ancient artifact photograph or rubbing was visually inspected. Available image descriptions establish modern redraw candidates only.

limitations.text: No image is proposed. The two supplied Commons oracle/bronze direct image URLs returned 404 during acquisition and are unavailable for this run. A separately inspected Commons seal-script file is described as a modern redraw and has a public-domain licensing statement, but its exact original-file fetch failed with a cache miss. The inspected Xiaoxuetang record supplies an oracle-form label, but the tool did not establish an accessible image with independently verified reuse terms for this submission.
